content.text: The licence architecture in § 13 satisfies every preferred element. Submitting a compliant finding without a redline.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: The Section 13 licence architecture meets the preferred position in full, so no redline is warranted. § 13.1 grants the subscription access right directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" — affiliates and contractors are named in the grant itself, with no notice or add-on gate, exceeding the fallback's "covered on written notice" standard. § 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, and § 14.3 pulls that perpetual licence through to Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable; § 10.1 confirms paid-up licences survive termination. § 13.3 bars Vendor from revoking or suspending a licence except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity, so the subscription licence is not revocable at will. § 13.3 also permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor tied to § 24.1, which allows assignment without Vendor consent to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, reinforced by § 24.4 (change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, or reprice). One point to note rather than flag: § 14.2 gives Customer only a "revocable, non-transferable licence" to a Deliverable during the Order Form term, which sits awkwardly with §§ 13.2 and 13.3. That is a Deliverable ownership/IP allocation point and is being raised under the IP rule; we do not flag the same term twice here.
